reason: The submitted CIF is parseable and explicit: its primitive P-1 cell (a=5.6375, b=5.8819, c=10.2166 A; alpha=90.829 degrees; V=338.739 A^3) symmetry-expands to 40 fully occupied atoms, Al2Ga4Bi2B8O24 (Z=2), with ordered Al/Ga/Bi sites. Indexing is strong (the trace indexes all 25 low-angle lines, and the CIF positions cover the 110 reported peaks within 0.025 degrees). The decisive atomic-coordinate evidence is nevertheless inadequate. The supplied comparable report has no score, the final response reports positions only, and the trace's final post-collision CIF has no reported final intensity residual. An independent restrained full-profile calculation of this exact CIF gives unweighted Rwp-like 0.374 (correlation 0.921), versus 0.082 for a Pawley-like independent-intensity fit on the same indexed lines; its profile SSE is 20.8 times the Pawley-like bound, with large errors on major reflections (for example near 17.95 degrees, observed about 75 versus calculated about 33 after global scaling). This is consistent with the trace's much poorer atomic-model normalized RMS of about 0.32 than its approximately 0.10 profile decomposition. Periodic chemistry also fails as a veto: complete shells contain Bi-O distances of 1.725 and 1.803 A and an O-O contact of 1.741 A, while an empirical bond-valence audit gives grossly incompatible valences (including Bi about 11.3 and one Ga about 2.1). Thus the indexed lattice is established but this instantiated framework/coordinate realization is not; another attempt is likely to produce a materially different viable atomic model. No specific alternative branch is yet supported strongly enough to identify.
